deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is part of the draft of Riemann's letter to Weierstrass dated Göttingen, 26 Oct 1859. It was printed in Crelle 71 (1870) as 'Beweis des Satzes, dass eine einwerthige mehr als 2n-fach periodische Function von n Veränderlichen unmöglich ist' and is in the Werke. Setting: f is a single-valued (holomorphic/meromorphic) function on C^n with period vectors a_mu = (a_mu^1,...,a_mu^n), mu = 1..2n. These are assumed R-linearly independent. Then x = sum_mu xi_mu a_mu with real coordinates xi_mu, and the half-open box P = {0 <= xi_mu < 1} is a fundamental domain for the lattice L = Z a_1 + ... + Z a_{2n}. The page completes two steps of the proof.

(A) Pigeonhole step (finishing the case where a_{2n+1} is not an integer combination, i.e. no relation sum_{mu=1}^{2n+1} m_mu a_mu = 0 with integers m).
- Take a point x_0 and its translates x_0 + k a_{2n+1}, k = 0,1,2,..., each reduced mod L into P.
- Under the assumption, these reduced points are pairwise distinct. So there are infinitely many points in P that are congruent modulo the group generated by a_1..a_{2n+1}.
- Divide each xi-interval [0,1) into q equal parts. This cuts P into q^{2n} cells, and within each cell every xi_mu varies by less than 1/q.
- Among more than q^{2n} such points, two lie in the same cell (Dirichlet's box principle). Their difference omega is a nonzero period of f whose real coordinates satisfy |xi_mu(omega)| <= 1/q for all mu.
- Since q is arbitrary, f has arbitrarily small nonzero periods.
- Riemann concludes that f, if continuous ('wenn sie stetig ist'), depends on fewer than n linear expressions in x, i.e. it is degenerate.
- Implicit step (mine): normalize omega_q / |omega_q| and pass to a limit direction v. Integer multiples of omega_q approximate every real multiple t v, so continuity gives f(x + t v) = f(x) for all real t. For holomorphic f, invariance along the real line R v forces invariance along the complex line C v. Hence f is a function of n-1 complex linear forms.

(B) Lemma for the remaining case, where there are n relations sum_{mu=1}^{2n+1} a_mu^nu m_mu = 0 with integer m. The goal is to show that the 2n+1 period systems are integer combinations of only 2n systems.

Sub-lemma (stated here, concluded on the next page): if m_1..m_{2n} are integers with gcd 1 and b_1 = sum m_mu a_mu, then one can find b_2..b_{2n} such that Z-span{a_mu} = Z-span{b_mu}. In modern terms, a primitive integer vector can be completed to a unimodular matrix (a basis of Z^{2n}).

Construction by the Euclidean algorithm:
- Let theta_1 = gcd(m_1, m_2) and choose integers alpha, beta with beta m_1 - alpha m_2 = theta_1.
- Define c_1 = (m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2)/theta_1 and b_{2n} = alpha a_1 + beta a_2.
- Then a_1 = beta c_1 - (m_2/theta_1) b_{2n} and a_2 = -alpha c_1 + (m_1/theta_1) b_{2n}.
- So the transformation matrix [[m_1/theta_1, m_2/theta_1], [alpha, beta]] has determinant 1. Hence span_Z{a_1, a_2} = span_Z{c_1, b_{2n}}, and congruence modulo one pair is the same as modulo the other.
- Iterate: with theta_2 = gcd(theta_1, m_3), set c_2 = (theta_1 c_1 + m_3 a_3)/theta_2 = (m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2 + m_3 a_3)/theta_2, and choose b_{2n-1} = alpha' c_1 + beta' a_3 with beta' theta_1 - alpha' m_3 = theta_2.
- Continuing, theta_{2n-1} = gcd(m_1..m_{2n}) = 1, so the last c equals b_1. The basis is then {b_1, b_2, ..., b_{2n}}.
- The next page notes that the covolume (volume of the period box) is unchanged. It then uses the lemma to reduce the relations to p b_1 = q a_{2n+1}, which leads to the reduction of covolume by the factor 1/q.
errors: Gap: in (A) Riemann says only 'wenn sie stetig ist'. Continuity alone gives invariance under a real one-parameter subgroup, i.e. dependence on fewer than 2n real linear forms. To get 'fewer than n linear expressions' (complex-linear), one needs holomorphy/analyticity, which is implicit in the setting of abelian functions.
Implicit step: passing from arbitrarily small periods to invariance under a whole line needs a compactness/limit argument on the directions of the small periods. This is not stated.

The distinctness of the infinitely many reduced points relies on the case assumption that no nonzero multiple of a_{2n+1} lies in the lattice of the first 2n periods. This is stated on the previous page, so it is not an error.

Possible notational slip: if the manuscript reads m_1/theta_1 in the formula for a_1 (the image is ambiguous), the correct coefficient is m_2/theta_1, as given in the transcription. Verified: a_1 = beta c_1 - (m_2/theta_1) b_{2n}.
The footnote assumption (R-independence of the 2n periods) is needed for the real coordinates xi. The degenerate case is waved away as 'leicht zu behandeln'.

results.what: Dirichlet box-principle argument: a group of periods of rank > 2n in C^n that is not reducible to 2n generators has arbitrarily small nonzero elements, so a continuous (holomorphic) function with these periods is degenerate
results.modern_name: Pigeonhole principle; non-discrete subgroups of R^{2n}; part of the theorem that a nondegenerate meromorphic function on C^n has a discrete period group of rank <= 2n
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi 1835 (n=1); Riemann (this letter, 1859, publ. 1870) and Weierstrass for general n; box principle Dirichlet 1842

results.what: Completion of a primitive integer vector (m_1..m_{2n}) to a unimodular basis via the Euclidean algorithm (successive gcd steps)
results.modern_name: Extension of a primitive vector to a basis of Z^n / unimodular completion (Hermite)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the draft of Riemann's published 1859 letter to Weierstrass (Crelle 71, 1870; Werke). Both the pigeonhole argument and the unimodular completion lemma are known and attributed to him in this context, and the lemma itself is standard number theory.

Equals 0: the inversion formula a_2 = -alpha c_1 + (m_1/theta_1) b_{2n} holds.
Equals 1: the basis change (a_1,a_2) -> (c_1,b_{2n}) is unimodular.

checkable.asserts: Both equal 0: the second Euclidean step (c_1,a_3) -> (c_2,b_{2n-1}) is invertible over Z.
Example: the primitive vector (2,3,5) completed to a unimodular matrix (det = 1), as the lemma guarantees.

transcription_corrections: Margin note keyed to the dagger probably reads '† in beiden zusammenfallen' or similar. It appears to be an insertion near 'derselben Grössen xi', but the reading is uncertain.
In the formula for a_1 the manuscript coefficient may be written m_1/theta_1. Mathematically it must be m_2/theta_1, as the transcription has it.
'[-gr-]' before 'von einander' is a struck-out false start ('gr...'), correctly marked as a deletion.
